title: Assassin (class)
snippet:
The Assassin Set has only moderate physical defences but has good magic and fire defences, and high overall resistances against anything that isn't Bleed.

While the **Assassin** doesn't have any ranged attack, its Spook Sorcery is extremely useful for removing most non-fatal fall damage and for completely silencing footsteps for 20 seconds, allowing certain obstacles to be bypassed . Unfortunately, while the starting Sorcerer's Staff is a fairly good spell tool, if not exactly the best, it won't actually start to gain scaling from stats until Intelligence has reached at least 19, delaying a possible strengthening of the character's Sorceries.

Picking up the Soul Arrow Sorcery from the Shrine Handmaid gives a reusable ranged attack early on, while the weapon buffing Magic Weapon Sorcery can be gained in either Undead Settlement or Road of Sacrifices to add some of a Staff's spellbuff to weapon damage.

title: Assassin (class)
snippet:
Assassin (class) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Assassin** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is a Dexterity-based class with decent Attunement for Weapon Arts and spells and some Intelligence for Sorceries.

An unusually long Thrusting Sword, the Estoc is also quite strong and has a rare sweeping heavy attack for hitting several or agile foes easier, at the cost of not having an increased critical modifier for Ripostes and Backstabs. Additionally, its Weapon Art, Shield Splitter, helps with its bad damage to the stamina of blocking targets by partially bypassing the defences of the block instead.

Its Targeting Shield, while not very suitable for blocking, is one of the game's three parrying shields and as such its Parry starts slightly earlier yet ends as late as the regular parry.

The Assassin Set has only moderate physical defences but has good magic and fire defences, and high overall resistances against anything that isn't Bleed.

snippet:
Most humanoid enemies can be backstabbed. Most enemies that can be parried and riposted can also be backstabbed. Some non-humanoid enemies, such as the Fang Boar in the Undead Parish (but not the ones in Anor Londo), can also be backstabbed, but generally non-humanoid enemies are impossible to backstab.

It is possible for two players or monsters to backstab a single target at once (each dealing their standard backstab damage). This requires precise timing and positioning, however.

title: Backstab
snippet:
Backstab -  Dark Souls - mechanic - general_information 
 general_information : Players may perform a backstab if they position themselves behind a humanoid enemy and do a light attack with shield down. Enemies must be on roughly the same level surface as the player. Backstabs can be performed with nearly every type of weapon, although exceptions exist (see below).

Backstabs deal high damage based on the damage of the weapon and its critical rate.

Backstabs cannot be interrupted. While in the motion of backstabbing, both the perpetrator and the victim are granted invincibility frames and cannot take further damage except for damage-over-time effects such as being poisoned, under the effects of toxic, or while using Power Within. An exception to invincibility frames is *Dark Souls II*, where you can still take damage during a backstab although the damage is reduced.

This is especially true of characters that use spell buffs as the damage buffs provide is determined mainly by the base AR of the weapon and affinity with infusions.

It has the same moveset as the Claymore, save for the strong attacks, which are overhead swings instead of thrusts. The fast attacks combine with the high Poise break to allow the weapon to stagger most enemies, including PvP opponents, with ease.

title: Critical attack
snippet:
Critical attack -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : In *Dark Souls III*, a critical attack can generally be performed on a target once it is put in a vulnerable state.

A **riposte** can be performed on a target that has had an attack parried, or has been guard broken due to stamina being completely depleted while guarding with a shield. In the case of certain large enemies and bosses, a critical can be taken once enough damage has been inflicted to a vital part of their body, or if enough damage has been inflicted in general.

A **backstab** can be performed on the target if they are attacked from behind. When the player is behind the target and performs a weak attack, they will begin an animation where they pull their weapon back in preparation to perform the critical. If the target is still within range of the player once the backstab animation completes, the critical attack will then take place.

title: Critical attack
snippet:
Critical attack -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : In *Dark Souls*, critical attacks do bonus damage based on a weapon's *critical* stat. Most weapons possess a critical multiplier of 100, but Thrusting Swords and Daggers have a higher critical multiplier, and thus do more damage when executing a critical attack.

Ripostes will do more bonus damage than backstabs, but can also be considerably harder to execute, as they need a parry or a guard-break to happen.

The plunging attack is the rarest and most damaging critical attack. For this strike a higher ground is required, in which the player must jump and while falling hit the normal attack button, thus making the plunge attack dependent on the terrain.

The Hornet Ring increases the damage of critical attacks by an additional 30%. Wearing the ring also changes the animation of backstabs and ripostes when using certain weapons against human enemies. Headshots are not affected by the Hornet Ring.

title: Critical attack
snippet:
Critical attack -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Critical attacks** (also known as **critical hits** or just **criticals**) are a gameplay mechanic in *Dark Souls*, *Dark Souls II* and *Dark Souls III*. Critical attacks are performed in what is considered the most vulnerable areas of enemies. There are four types of critical attacks: backstabs, ripostes, headshots and plunging attacks.

title: Critical attack
snippet:
Upon successfully initiating a critical, the player and target are both placed in an uninterruptible animation where both parties cannot take damage from outside sources, and the target takes the critical damage. Both parties will only be able to perform additional actions once the critical animation is complete.

Damage inflicted by the critical can be increased if the player has equipped the Hornet Ring. If the target is wearing the Dragonscale Ring, damage from a backstab critical is decreased.

Handled as a blend between greatswords and ultra greatswords, the Curved Greatsword class are weapons that excel at damage output with speeds comparable to that of smaller weapons. Boasting relatively fast one-handed, horizontal swings, and vertical, two-handed swings, which can vary in speeds when used as a follow-up attack. title: Daggers (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Daggers (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - weapon - lead 
 lead : **Daggers** are a type of weapon in *Dark Souls II*.

Daggers are usually the go-to weapon when it comes to critical attacks against enemies, even though a majority of them deal average damage with both backstabs and parried ripostes to enemy players. Some daggers, such as the Bandit's Knife or the Umbral Dagger, deal more damage with a backstab than usual, while others like the Shadow Dagger or the Manikin Knife, deal more damage with a parried riposte.

However, what does set the daggers apart from other weapons is all of them have a strong modifier on a guard-broken player or enemy that is then riposted with one, dealing nearly twice as much damage as they would with a backstab or parried riposte. This makes a dagger a very reliable weapon against enemies known to defend themselves often with a shield or their weapon, allowing for a powerful, and punishing, critical attack against them.

title: Parry and Riposte
snippet: Parrying does not always succeed, and requires precise timing. A parry that is executed too early or too late will grant the player some super armor, as well as some damage reduction from the attack that the player attempted to parry, but will not cause the opponent to be stunned or vulnerable to riposting. This type of parrying is often known as "partial parrying". Unlike full parries, partial parries can be used against almost any attack encountered in the game. Rarely, it is possible to both do a successful parry and still take damage. Parrying most often succeeds when the player is standing very close to his or her opponent, and on relatively even ground.

 new_features : Listed below are some minor differences found in *Dark Souls II*, which may be slightly confusing to those who mastered these techniques in the original *Dark Souls* game.
In *Dark Souls II*, there is no temporary invincibility when parrying or riposting, but any damage received while performing these moves will be considerably less than normal (about 90% reduction).
The timing of a parry in *Dark Souls II* is different: it must be initiated when the enemy's attack animation begins, if parrying fast and medium weapons (daggers, straight swords, curved swords, etc.) or mid-swing, if parrying slow weapons (ultra greatswords, great hammers, etc.). Ammunition must first be equipped in the menu to either one of the Arrow Slots for Arrows and Greatarrows or the Bolts Slots for Bolts.  general_information : Grabs are unblockable, special attacks that can be performed by specific enemies and bosses. Although un-blockable, they are often telegraphed in advance and once recognized can, in most cases, be easily dodged.

Backstabbing and Riposting can be thought of as types of grab attacks and, like grabs performed by enemies, usually can't be interrupted and the initiator and the victim are invulnerable to outside interaction. title: Poise (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Poise (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - hyper_armor 
 hyper_armor : Hyper Armor is a state a player or NPC can access, usually via specific weapon attacks, which changes how Poise Damage interacts with them.

When Hyper Armor is active, attacks a character receives are altered in two ways:
Hyperstagger gets ignored.
Incoming Poise Damage is reduced.
This way, attacks that can hyper stagger get countered by attacks from heavy weapons and characters that use them can make more use of Poise than characters with lighter weapons can.

Each weapon has a specific Hyper Armor multiplier that corresponds to its weapon class. Weapon class doesn't entirely correlate with the menu 's specified class but rather with the moveset of the weapon.

Not all attacks apply hyper armor, as a general rule it's limited to the slower attacks on weapons.

Dodge rolls have a similar mechanic where they simply ignore poise damage for a section of their animation after their iframes end.

snippet:
Lothric Knight -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Lothric Knights possess a significant amount of health and are aggressive fighters; however, most of their attacks are easy to dodge through and can easily be backstabbed by dodging behind them at the end of any of their attack chains. They are susceptible to parries, and by kicking when their shields are raised or one too many attacks are absorbed, one can score a critical hit after breaking their guard.

They utilize various weapon arts depending upon what they wield. For instance, the straight sword-wielding knights can perform a broad, horizontal slash that inflicts heavy stamina damage if blocked, and a vicious lunge attack that is surprisingly fast and deals heavy damage whilst potentially knocking the player down.

title: Engorged Hollow
snippet:
Engorged Hollow -  Dark Souls - enemy - strategies 
 strategies : There will be no visible cloud of blood if the engorged hollow is killed with Fire damage and toxic discharge range will be extremely short in this case. However, if the player is pressed in very close for the killing blow, they can still be hit with toxic.

Since the Toxic discharge has a very short range, the use of a ranged or long handled weapon, like a Spear or Halberd, is very effective.

Backstabbing will delay the Toxin's release; however, the blood must still be avoided for a few seconds. Parrying and riposting will not work for avoiding the toxin.

Attacking with a Spear or Thrusting Sword while simultaneously blocking with the Spider Shield will block the toxic discharge.

A lethal attack with significant knockback, such as the Black Knight Greatsword's power attacks, will in general keep the toxic cloud away from the player.

title: Scimitar (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Scimitar (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Scimitar is a light and fast weapon that excels at chaining together numerous small attacks to quickly stack up damage on its target. Its attacks are fast with very short delays, but this is countered by having rather short range, requiring the wielder to get in close with the enemy. These characteristics help the Scimitar to define the "light curved sword" moveset that it shares with its lighter brethren.

The drawback of the Scimitar is that while it can chain together numerous small attacks, it lacks the heavier punch required to prevail against armored foes. Its strong attacks are simply chains of weak attacks, as is its skill. As well, it does not possess a kick, but rather a quick slash that can be used to create distance from a foe; this prevents the weapon from being used to break the guard of a shield.

title: Soul of Cinder
snippet:
Soul of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - phase_1 
 phase_1 : Soul of Cinder can use four different weapon stances, each utilizing different skills and attacks based on a magic type in the game (excluding hexes).
***Standard (straight sword)**: It's default stance combines quick slashes and thrust attacks at range. Utilizes two unique weapon skills, one being an enhanced version of "stance", a "guard breaking" slash with increased range, and another which is two slow, but powerful, spin attacks.
***Scimitar/Pyromancy**: Quick, horizontal slashes and wound-up vertical slashes, and a quick, evasive slash or backflip to avoid attacks and can parry attacks and deliver a riposte. Also uses a combination of many offensive pyromancies, including Power Within, Great Combustion, Great Chaos Fire Orb and Poison Mist.

title: Fume Knight
snippet:
Fume Knight -  Dark Souls II - boss - attacks 
 attacks : **Backward Slash:** Used when the player is standing to Raime's right or left. He will quickly slash down and back with either his greatsword or the longsword, always using the weapon on the side where the player is standing. Very little tell, can be difficult to dodge. He will do the same move when in his second phase as well, only this time it is more powerful with a higher starting lag.

**Four-hit combo:** Raime will use the longsword in a three-hit combo, likely draining a lot of stamina if blocking and possibly guard-breaking the player. This can be dangerous as he can follow up the longsword attacks with a long, slow horizontal greatsword slash that deals high damage.

title: Farron Flashsword
snippet:
With a high pool of Intelligence, the damage of each slash can be on par with what a Crystal-infused straight sword is capable of. These traits allow sorcerers to have a reliable, and effective, close-quarters tool for dispatching of foes that close in on them, instead of having to run the risk of using ranged Sorceries at close range. Mixing Farron Flashsword with Soul Greatsword is an effective way to deal with aggressive enemies, and in terms of PvP, disorient or otherwise catch players off-guard.

However, there is a catch to using this sorcery; since it behaves like a straight sword when in use, it is able to be parried much like one. This should be taken into consideration before engaging an enemy that can parry the caster or dons a parrying shield.

title: Homing Soulmass
snippet:
The main weakness of Soulmasses is that the timing at which they fire cannot be controlled. This makes it somewhat ineffective against melee enemies using shields, as it tends to fire while they are guarding, doing significantly reduced damage, whereas other projectile sorceries can be timed to hit when the enemy goes into an animation in which their guard is down. Another weakness of Soulmassess is that when fighting larger opponents, such as the Bounding Demon of Izalith, the spell will activate prematurely and expire before reaching the target's actual hitbox unless the player or the target run towards each other.

Against ranged attack enemies, and many bosses, who don't use shields, the spell is extremely effective, as the player can focus on blocking or dodging while it fires, and prepare new Soulmasses while in cover or between attacks. This is particularly useful in the fight against Dragonslayer Ornstein and Executioner Smough, for example.

title: Halberds
snippet:
Halberds -  Dark Souls - weapon - overview 
 overview : Halberds offer a mixture of the spears' range and thrusting attacks, along with a bladed edge similar to an axe for attacks that deal Regular or Slash damage. Because of the increased weight at the end of the weapon, however, the attacks are not quite as precise as they are with a Spear, and each swing tends to take one slightly off balance. Most of the spears' quick strikes are lost too, in favor of slower, but slightly more powerful attacks. The ability to use a variety of attack types at range, however, can be a very useful thing, as it enables one to be effective against most types of enemies.

All halberds besides the Scythe, Great Scythe, and Lifehunt Scythe deal Thrust damage on their weak attacks and are therefore eligible for counter attack bonuses.

title: Charred Loyce Knight
snippet:
A two-handed basic attack using a weapon with a 35 Poise-breaking rating is guaranteed to stagger a Charred Loyce Knight, so long as they have not been buffed due to the presence of a summon (if fighting the Burnt Ivory King); long weapons such as spears and halberds can help in keeping them from getting too close. If a knight is interrupted during their running attack, they may backstep if they are hit less than three times in succession, though they may chain this into a running counter-attack or even a jumping attack.

The Charred Loyce Knights will occasionally use their shields to block attacks, especially the pyromancer knight. However, they have relatively little stability and a few attacks will usually result in a guard break. While the knights cannot be backstabbed, they can be frontal-riposted during the guard break, which allows them to be quickly and easily dispatched.

title: Target Shield (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Target Shield (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Target Shield has relatively low requirements to wield, though unlike most other shields it requires at least a small amount of investment in Dexterity. Like other Small Shields, it does not provide very much protection when used to block attacks.

What sets the Target Shield apart from its peers is that it is one of three Parrying Shields in the game, along with the Small Leather Shield and the Buckler, with active parrying frames starting up faster than on most other Small Shields. In this regard, the Target Shield provides the best of both worlds, possessing a higher stability and physical absorption than the other two Parrying Shields, which allows it to somewhat safeguard its wielder from attacks.

title: Weapon Types (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Weapon Types (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - weapon - hammers 
 hammers : ;Hammers
Hammers are slow weapons designed for single, powerful strikes. If the enemy staggers, however, another strike can usually connect. Hammers, oddly, are about evenly split between Striking and Thrust attacks.

;Great Hammers
Great Hammers are very slow weapons with good range designed for heavy strikes. All of the Great Hammers are immensely heavy, and this weight is used in large, powerful swings.

title: Hollow Soldier (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Spear wielding soldiers use mostly lunging attacks with little tracking so they can be easily dodged by strafing to the side, however they can perform a sweeping attack.

Estoc wielding soldiers strike at a medium speed and occasionally in a combo. Sometimes they will use their shield to guard. They are also capable of parrying the player.

title: Weapons (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Weapons (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - item - attack_types_and_parameters 
 attack_types_and_parameters : All weapons have an Attack Type, otherwise known as a damage type, and can have values in Physical, Magic, Fire, and Lightning damage. Some weapons have varying movesets, or attacks, and each move may inflict a different type of physical damage. For example, some daggers inflict Slash or Thrust damage depending on which attack is used.

Weapons have parameters, also called stat requirements that need to be met in order to be wielded properly. These are usually Strength and Dexterity but can also include Intelligence or Faith. If the Strength stat isn't met, two-handing the weapon will decrease the requirement, effectively increasing the player's Strength by a factor of 1.5. Many weapons also have parameter bonuses that scale with corresponding attributes, providing a higher attack rating.

title: Greatlance
snippet:
Greatlance -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The strong attacks have the ability to hit enemies multiple times. The lance's general feature of each attack advancing the player forward can be used to punish retreating players, however, due to the buildup before each strike, the greatlance is easily avoided and dodged in most scenarios, making it inadequate for PvP.

For PvP, if you can land a weak attack while two-handing or using a shield allowing use for a weapon art while one-handing, you can follow up the weak attack with the weapon art which hits multiple times.

title: Desert Sorceress
snippet:
Desert Sorceress -  Dark Souls II - enemy - attacks 
 attacks : **Scattering Flame**
The Sorceress launches a volley of five fireballs into the air, which then arc downward, hitting the ground and exploding. The blasts are quite large and the damage from multiple flames can quickly prove fatal if a player is unfortunate enough to be in the area of multiple blasts. Fortunately, the flames explode on impact, which means they frequently fail to reach their full potential due to hitting the ceiling or walls. Their high arc and wide spread also allows players to step between the fireballs, or simply run under them harmlessly.

title: Marvelous Chester
snippet:
Marvelous Chester -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : Marvellous Chester does not use a regular player model, instead using a completely unique model and animation rig. This technique is used for Anastacia and Andre of Astora and for many of the NPCs featured in *Dark Souls II*.
**The special Hornet Ring animation will not play when parrying/backstabbing Chester, nor can the Dark Hand be used to drain humanity from him like with every other human NPC.
**This may also be the reason why he is the only invader encountered in the game that does not leave a Bloodstain upon being defeated.
He is the only other invader besides Kirk, Knight of Thorns who can be defeated more than once per playthrough.
**Unlike Kirk, who can only invade three times in the entire game, Marvellous Chester will invade indefinitely unless his human form is killed.

title: Hydra
snippet:
Hydra -  Dark Souls - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : The Hydra can be defeated by severing its heads or by targeting the main body and using ranged attacks.

As the player moves closer to the shore, the Hydra will almost exclusively use its head strikes. After it lunges toward the player, each head will bury itself in the ground for a short time, presenting an opportunity to sever its vulnerable necks. As each head is defeated, the spread of the Hydra's attacks will diminish, making it easier for the player to finish the job.

The lunge attacks can be blocked or dodged. Certain spots can be found where the heads will completely miss the player. If the Hydra's position does not change, these spots can be exploited throughout the battle.

title: Physical (damage type)
snippet:
Physical (damage type) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - general_information 
 general_information : There are four forms of physical damage: Regular (absent from *Dark Souls II*), Strike, Slash and Thrust. Each have a corresponding defense stat that they are measured against. Because of this, certain physical damage may be ineffective against certain enemies, while other forms will be very effective.

What damage type a particular weapon deals varies and can be determined by toggling a weapon's display and looking under "Attack Type". Many weapons will display two types of physical damage. Which one is dealt is dependent on which attack of its moveset is used.

Physical damage is encountered most commonly out of all the damage types when facing enemies and can also be encountered in the form of traps.

Any Dexterity or Strength scaling a weapon possesses goes to its physical damage.

All shields reduce a high percentage of physical damage, many of them 100%.

title: Aged Smelter Sword
snippet:
Aged Smelter Sword -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Visually, its design is very similar to the Smelter Sword. The only difference is that it glows blue, as it deals Magic damage, as opposed to Fire damage.

Whilst being one of the heaviest weapons in the game, the Aged Smelter Sword features a unique moveset, where each strong attack is a combustion-inducing strike, creating a small, fiery explosion when the sword makes contact. Strong attacks consume 10 durability each; this can be partially mitigated with use of the Bracing Knuckle Ring variants. Unlike most boss soul weapons, the Aged Smelter Sword cannot be infused.

title: Effigy Shield
snippet:
Effigy Shield -  Dark Souls - shield - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Effigy Shield has the highest defense against lightning of any shield in the game which unfortunately is not affected by the Lightning Upgrade Path. It has light deflection and normal parry speed. The crystal durability is 18.

This shield can be used without meeting the Faith requirement, as with the Sanctus. The Faith requirement only applies if it's used as a weapon. Blocking and parrying remain unhindered; however, the stability will be penalized, increasing the likelihood that the player's guard will break.

title: Stagger Damage
snippet:
Stagger Damage -  Dark Souls - mechanic - execution 
 execution : Inflicting stagger damage can be achieved in the following ways:
Attacking after deflecting an enemy's attack with a shield or when the attack is deflected by a wall.
Attacking after parrying, but in a position where riposting does not occur.
Attacking after kicking an enemy.
Attacking a blocking enemy that has run out of stamina.

The attack must be carried out in a relatively small window of time, which can vary depending on the enemy, for the damage bonus to take effect.

title: Power Stance
snippet:
Power Stance -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - compatibility_chart 
 compatibility_chart : The following chart represents all powerstancing categories the game accepts as usable. These are placed in order of Preference given to them for the mechanic. The closer the weapon class is to the top left corner, the less Preference they are given. The 3 categories are represented thus:

- : Non Compatible. These pairings cannot be powerstanced.
1: Same Types: These pairings have equal Preference and thus which attacks are used is determined by the right hand weapon.
2: Different Types: These pairings have different Preference, thus the weapon with more Preference will always determine the attacks used.

These Categories are generally determined by moveset, not the weapon class displayed in the menu. For example, Crypt Blacksword is considered a Greataxe despite saying Ultra Greatsword in the menu. Lists of each category are found on this page.

title: Small Leather Shield (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Small Leather Shield (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : With a low stat requirement and very light weight, the Small Leather Shield can be easily equipped by most any build in the game for almost no consequence. As it is a Small Shield, it provides pitiful defense when used to block attacks, even after upgrades.

However, it is one of three shields in the game (along with the Buckler and the Target Shield) classified as a Parrying Shield, with active parry frames that begin sooner than those of other Small Shields. This makes it an ideal tool for parrying enemy attacks on reaction, rather than on prediction.

title: Lothric Knight Greatshield
snippet:
Lothric Knight Greatshield -  Dark Souls III - weapon - description 
 description : Greatshield of the renowned Lothric Knights, decorated with a holy symbol.

The knights who formed the High Priestess' guard carried greatshields such as these, which were granted high magic absorption through her blessing.

Skill: Shield Bash
Without lowering your guard, strike the enemy with the shield to knock them back or stagger them. Works while equipped in either hand.

title: Gauntlets
snippet:
Gauntlets -  Dark Souls - weapon - overview 
 overview : Gauntlets have by far the shortest range of all the weapon types in *Dark Souls*, which means they require getting up close and personal with the enemy. They make up for their limited range with their speed. They can attack extremely fast, being able to create long chains of relentless attacks as long as the player's stamina holds out. Gauntlets are one of the few weapon classes that have the ability to parry when used in the left hand.

With a gauntlet weapon (including fists) equipped in the right hand, the kick animation is changed - rather than a heel kick, the character strikes with the knee. This does not seem to affect the function or range of the kick.

title: Fire Witch
snippet:
Fire Witch -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Fire Witches use several different pyromancies that can cause heavy damage if the player is caught in them. They will usually switch between conjuring a trail of fire directly at the player or creating a single pillar of flame under their feet. Both of these attacks can be used from a long distance and can hit the player even if they are behind cover.

These enemies often appear with Pontiff Knights and Irithyllian Slaves, which makes them challenging to engage directly. It is recommended to take out the accompanying foes before dealing with the Witches themselves, as the player can easily be staggered by other attacks, leaving them open to the Witch's pyromancy.

title: Watcher Greatsword
snippet:
Watcher Greatsword -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Similar to the Defender Greatsword, the Watcher Greatsword's special attack is a unique weapon buff, which is triggered by wielding it in both hands and pressing the Parry button. Rather than a lightning buff, however, the Watcher Greatsword can buff itself with magic.

This buff costs 10 durability each time, meaning it can be used up to five times until breaking. However, the use of the Bracing Knuckle Ring variants reduces the cost of the buff (depending on the level of the ring used), allowing the buff to be used more before breaking the weapon.

In addition to the buff adding magic damage, its fairly low physical stat requirements make it a practical choice for characters with high Intelligence. This, along with its lower weight, stat requirements, faster swing speed, and overall superior scaling makes it a much better choice than the Moonlight Greatsword for high Intelligence builds.

title: Parrying Dagger
snippet:
Parrying Dagger -  Dark Souls - weapon - trivia 
 trivia : Characters that use this weapon (such as Lautrec and the Darkmoon Knightess) can block with the Parrying Dagger one-handed; however this action is not available for the player.

title: Weapon Types (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Weapon Types (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - weapon - polearms 
 polearms : ;Spears
Spears are excellent weapons for tactical combat, as most Spears' one-handed light attacks can be used while still blocking and their range is impressive. However, their thrusting attacks only have a small hitbox so they are easily dodged. Spear players must take special care to let down their shield to recover stamina and avoid a guard break. Spears are best used to hold position in a narrow corridor and are a poor choice for agile or small enemies. Although Spears mostly do thrust damage, their rolling attacks actually deal strike damage, making them very effective against heavily armored enemies. As this weapon type is a polearm, one must hit with the tip of the Spear to deal maximum damage, and so this requires players to maintain their distance from the enemy.

title: Shields (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Shields (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - item - lead 
 lead : **Shields** are a type of equipment in *Dark Souls III*. They serve the primary function of being used defensively, allowing for the blocking of incoming attacks from enemies. Much like any normally wielded weapon, they have special skills that can serve a variety of purposes, such as Parrying, shield bashing, and allowing the player to use a weapon skill directly from the guard.
